_comment: Ratchet down only — lower a number when a real fix reduces that count. Never raise one to make a red run green (enforced by testBaselineRatchet() against the git HEAD-committed copy of this file, which since cycle 2 stage 8 skips non-numeric keys like this one). Originally measured 2026-09-03 by test/frontend.test.js (Milestone 1, the harness itself). Re-measured cycle 0 stage 5, two steps: (1) htmlValidateErrors 57->49 by deleting the orphan <path> fragment at index.html:15 that broke the <head>/<body> boundary; axeViolations_auth (5, contaminated by a leaked profile panel behind an unclosed modal, and mislabelled since showAuth('login') actually rendered 'welcome') replaced by axeViolations_authWelcome/authLogin (1/1, the real numbers once the surface actually opens A.ui.openPanel(null) first and clicks through to the login form). (2) htmlValidateErrors 49->13 by adding type=button to all 32 static buttons, aria-label to #btn-avatar, role=region/group -> converted to <section>/kept role=group on #race-hud and #radar-dock, and converting #radar-alerts to <section>; #search-results stayed a div[role=listbox] on purpose (real keyboard-driven ARIA combobox, see the comment in index.html). Per plan amendment §5(b), the remaining 13 (7 void-style self-closing tags, 5 no-inline-style, 1 prefer-native-element for the intentional listbox) are lint-preset taste, not defects, and are the new floor for this rule-class metric. Re-measured cycle 2 stage 8: axeViolations_shell/nearby/authWelcome/authLogin 1->0 by converting #radar-dock from div[role=group] to <section aria-label> (a real landmark), the single element responsible for the 'region' violation on all six surfaces; axeViolations_convoy 2->0 and axeViolations_profile 5->0 by giving mkRow()/mkField() (js/ui.js) real accessible-name wiring (aria-labelledby / label-for with never-resetting id counters) instead of a visually-adjacent-but-unassociated label, adding aria-label to the two .dot-color color-swatch inputs (title alone is a weak WCAG fallback), and adding aria-label+aria-pressed to the .emoji-btn rider-insignia and convoy-flag icon pickers (abstract glyphs with no discernible text before this). htmlValidateErrors and detectorWarnings untouched this stage (out of scope — see stage 8 report). Re-measured cycle 2 stage 10 (first CSS-touching stage of the mission): detectorWarnings 37->17. Step 1: raised every font-size below 12px in css/styles.css to a 12px floor (76 declarations), clearing undersized-ui-text (14->0) and tiny-text (1->0); detector 37->22. Step 2: converted the 5 progress-bar fills (.progress i, .vc-meter-fill, .rrisk-fill, .dragy-prog i, .race-row-bar i) from animating width to animating transform:scaleX() (compositor-only, avoids layout thrash — .vc-meter-fill re-renders every 60ms during voice activity), updating all 5 JS writers (js/routing.js:1182, js/ui.js:2572, js/radar.js:593, js/dragy.js:397, js/race.js:362) in the same commit; clearing layout-transition (5->0); detector 22->17. The remaining 17 (dark-glow 6, side-tab 4, codex-grid-background 2, gpt-thin-border-wide-shadow 2, repeating-stripes-gradient 1, clipped-overflow-container 2) are checked-in design-identity decisions, not defects — see css/DESIGN-DECISIONS.md. Two items are visual-verification-pending (no browser on this box, see STATE.md): the .rd-limit span 'LIMIT' caption grew from 8px to 12px and may widen past its 46px min-width badge (acceptable per the improvement directive, min-width not max-width so it grows rather than clips); the .progress i / .dragy-prog i box-shadow glows are horizontally compressed by scaleX(s) at partial fill (reasoned as a subtle delta on a 5-6px bar, not seen). Cycle 57 stage 46 (aspect C, milestone C1): three boot-cost keys added by testBootCost() — bootAssetRequests (index.html + every same-origin script/stylesheet it references), bootAssetGzipBytes (zlib level 9 over those assets plus index.html with its ?v= stamps normalised to cy000, so a stamp bump cannot move it) and bootExternalOrigins (distinct hosts across every <script src>/<link href>, preconnect hints included). Pinned at what the tree measured that stage (46 / 357743 / 5); the cycle-56 improve stage measured the same tree in a real headless Chromium at 46 requests, ~348 KB gzip and 705 ms DOMContentLoaded. Reducing them is plan v1 M7 / aspect E1 (the ui.js split), never a bundler. A Node/zlib upgrade that shifts gzip output by a few bytes is the one legitimate reason to re-measure bootAssetGzipBytes; say so in the stage report if it happens. Cycle 58 stage 50 (aspect C, milestone C2): bootAssetGzipBytes (357743, pinned at the exact measurement with zero headroom) retired for bootAssetGzipBudget = 359424 — the seat-resume client (js/net.js grace window + token echo, js/party.js gate) measured 359345, rounded UP to the next whole KiB (351 KiB). Rule: this budget moves up only with a named, justified retirement written into the stage report and here; the aspect-C target is <= 300 KB, so it is meant to trend DOWN, and the next stage that adds more than the 79 B of headroom must make the same conscious decision again. A retired key never silently reappears higher (testBaselineRatchet skips retired keys; precedent axeViolations_auth -> authWelcome/authLogin, cycle 8). Cycle 60 stage 59 (aspect C, milestone C4a): bootAssetGzipBudget ratcheted DOWN 359424 -> 358400 — deleting the unreachable solo physics from js/sim.js (BUGS.md frontend-003: never reachable since the initial commit, 802 -> 645 lines) took the measurement from 359408 to 357786, so the next whole KiB is 358400 with 614 B of headroom for cycle 61+ (a ratchet-down needs no _raised entry; the retirement rule above still governs any move up). Mission 20260903-173653-75d3 cycle 0 improve stage: bootAssetGzipBudget raised 358400 -> 359424, a named, justified move UP per the rule above — two real bug fixes landed in the same stage that legitimately cost bytes: (1) js/mapview.js's init() no longer throws synchronously when MapLibre's CDN script hasn't loaded (it now returns Promise.reject(e) instead), which makes js/app.js:63's crash-report .catch() reachable for the first time — previously dead code for its most likely trigger; (2) js/routing.js's probeTts() moved from a parse-time call (a GET /api/tts/health round-trip on the boot path for an answer nothing needs for minutes) to firing on the first A.store 'route' event, and js/telemetry.js's first flush now waits for window 'load' + an idle tick before arming (T1.4, the mission's first measured boot-path win: verified apiCalls:0 with a working map, see the stage report for why the standard externally-blackholed bench still shows 1-2 — an unrelated, correct side effect of fix (1)). Measured 359121, rounded UP to the next whole KiB (351 KiB) per the existing convention — 303 B of headroom for the next stage. The aspect-C/P-B target (<= 300 KB) is unchanged and still meant to trend down from here. Mission 20260903-173653-75d3 cycle 2 stage (T1.5a, directive task 4): bootAssetRequests ratcheted DOWN 46 -> 45 and bootAssetGzipBudget ratcheted DOWN 359424 -> 345088 by taking js/data.js (the static vehicle/paint/name/city catalog, 16197 B gzip) off the boot path entirely — index.html no longer has a <script src=js/data.js> tag; js/config.js seeds A.data = A.data || {} so js/ui.js's and js/party.js's parse-time `var D = A.data` capture is never undefined; js/data.js now MUTATES that same object (for..in copy, never reassigns) and sets A.data.loaded = true; A.data.ensure() (js/config.js, cached promise) injects the script lazily, warmed once at load+idle from js/app.js and additionally awaited at the two D-heavy panel entry points (buildProfilePanel's garage branch; buildGaragePage runs only after that await resolves) so a rider who beats the idle warm still gets a populated garage instead of empty dropdowns. Measured 344549, rounded UP to the next whole KiB (337 KiB = 345088) per the existing convention — 539 B of headroom for the next stage. This is the mission's first real byte-budget win (P-B): 359424 -> 345088, -14336 B / -1 request. Target is still <= 300 KB. Mission 20260903-173653-75d3 cycle 3 stage (task 3): bootAssetRequests ratcheted DOWN 45 -> 44 and bootAssetGzipBudget ratcheted DOWN 345088 -> 330752 by taking js/voice.js (walkie-talkie, 15620 B gzip) off the boot path the same way js/data.js left in cycle 2 — index.html no longer has a <script src=js/voice.js> tag; js/config.js's new A.voiceLoader.ensure() (built on the task-1/2 hardened A.util.loadOnce(), which also now retries on a failed load instead of caching a rejected promise forever — the reviewer's cycle-2 finding) lazily injects it; js/app.js warms it once at load+idle (same shape as A.data) and calls A.voice.init() in that .then(); js/voice.js's init() now calls reconcile() once immediately so a late (lazy) init does not ignore a convoy that already formed before the idle warm resolved; js/ui.js's buildVoiceSettings() awaits A.voiceLoader.ensure() (with the same generation-counter + DOM-identity re-entrancy guard as buildProfilePanel's task-2 fix) before rendering, degrading to the capability-stripped section on a failed load exactly as it already did for a voice module that never loaded at all. Measured 330662 (up from the directive's ~328929 estimate by ~1733 B — the extra cost of task 1/2's retry-on-rejection loader and two re-entrancy guards, real correctness fixes bundled into the same stage per the directive's own sequencing, not slippage), rounded UP to the next whole KiB (323 KiB = 330752) per the existing convention — 90 B of headroom for the next stage. Target is still <= 300 KB. Mission 20260903-173653-75d3 cycle 4 stage (directive task 3): bootAssetRequests ratcheted DOWN 44 -> 42 and bootAssetGzipBudget ratcheted DOWN 330752 -> 311296 by taking js/radar.js (Ghost-radar HUD, 15079 B gzip) and js/scanners.js (OpenMHz police-scanner directory, 5722 B gzip) off the boot path together, on a new generic factory (A.lazy.module(key, check), js/config.js) generalising the A.data.ensure()/A.voiceLoader.ensure() shape from cycles 2-3: index.html no longer has <script src=js/radar.js> or <script src=js/scanners.js> tags. js/scanners.js's only entry point (its own self-wired #chip-scan click listener) is unchanged; js/ui.js's init() adds a shim listener on the same chip that loads the module on first tap, runs A.ui.legalGate exactly as the module runs on itself, then removes its own listener so a later tap (after the module has self-wired) does not double-fire the gate. js/radar.js's five entry points (js/ui.js's two Ghost-Mode A.radar.setActive sites, js/native.js's three BLE-detector-alert sites) now go through A.lazy.radar() -- the two js/native.js sites are alerting paths (guardrail 6), so they pull the module in on first alert rather than dropping it via a naive `if (A.radar)` guard, which would have silently broken alerts for a rider who never turned Ghost Mode on. Measured 310725 (assets gzip 304353 + index.html gzip 6372), rounded UP to the next whole KiB (304 KiB = 311296) per the existing convention -- 571 B of headroom for the next stage. This lands P-B's headline metric target (<= 300 KB / 307200 B) within one more small module. Mission 20260903-173653-75d3 cycle 5 stage (directive tasks 2-3): bootAssetRequests ratcheted DOWN 42 -> 40 and bootAssetGzipBudget ratcheted DOWN 311296 -> 296960 by taking js/race.js (drag-race lobby/HUD client, 6715 B gzip) and js/dragy.js (GPS drag timer, 8513 B gzip) off the boot path on the same A.lazy.module() factory: index.html no longer has <script src=js/race.js> or <script src=js/dragy.js> tags. A.lazy.race (js/config.js) depends on A.lazy.dragy and loads it FIRST -- js/race.js's modeById() falls back to A.racetimer.modeById, which only js/dragy.js ever publishes (js/dragy.js:500), so a race started by a rider who never opened the dragy chip would otherwise resolve no mode and silently never begin (Trap A, closed by test/lazydata.test.js's checkRaceLoadsDragyDependencyTrapA). js/net.js's three inbound race:state/race:invite/race:fix handlers now route through A.lazy.race().then(...).catch(()=>{}) instead of a naive `if (A.race)` guard -- they are alerting/message paths (guardrail 6), so a message that arrives before the module loads pulls it in rather than being silently dropped (test/lazydata.test.js's checkRaceInviteNotDropped, proven RED against the pre-task net.js by git-stash). js/ui.js's 'Challenge to race' button (public profile overlay) used to be gated on A.race already being loaded -- it now renders unconditionally and loads the module on click. A new #chip-dragy shim in js/ui.js's init() mirrors #chip-scan's, written with the fix for a real reviewer MEDIUM found and fixed in the same stage: the #chip-scan shim removed its listener inside the .then() (after the load resolved), so two rapid taps before the load settled both attached a .then() and both fired the legal gate; the fix removes the listener SYNCHRONOUSLY at the top of the handler (before the async chain starts) and only re-attaches it in .catch() so a failed load can still be retried -- applied to both #chip-scan and the new #chip-dragy shim, and proven RED against the pre-fix #chip-scan shim by git-stash (gateCalls=2 before, =1 after). buildProfilePanel()'s existing profileGen-guarded await now covers js/dragy.js too (main view awaits A.lazy.dragy() for renderTimes()'s human mode labels/sort order; garage view still only awaits A.data.ensure(), which is all it ever read) and openProfileOverlay() re-renders the public overlay in place via the existing profileOverlayId guard once js/dragy.js resolves. Measured 296745 (assets gzip 290382 + index.html gzip 6363), rounded UP to the next whole KiB (290 KiB = 296960) per the existing convention -- 215 B of headroom. This is the first cycle bootAssetGzipBudget has measured UNDER the mission's <= 300 KB / 307200 B target (10,240 B of margin at the pin).
